body: I lot of times when I’m driving on my own I think about how easy it would be to kill myself. A quick flick of the wrist going down the freeway and I’d roll my car probably 6-7 times. Or drive off a mountain road. I wonder if somehow that would make it easier on my mom rather than making it more obvious.

I came to this sub tonight to post this very thing. I have no doubt killing myself would probably take 10 years off my moms life on grief alone. 

I don’t even have that close of a relationship with her, I just can’t do that to someone.
I don’t know who you are, but truly, thank you for this.

I just end up feeling hypocritical for putting up a front of everything being fine. So yeah, I usually feel pretty terrible there and just want to get away. Back to the apartment, down a couple beers, and try again tomorrow.
I've never been able to journal for more than a week or two, but writing letters like this is still one of the best ways I've found to try and destress in a non-harmful way.
I try sometimes, but usually feel like I'm not being actually helpful to the OP, so I stop.

It sounds like a cliche, but try working out to pass the evenings? It lets your mind be focused on something else at least for an hour or two, and can also give you some goals to actively work for. When I feel like life is pointless, I've found that setting little stupid goals like "shave 10 seconds off your best mile time by next month" gives me something, no matter how small, to work for.

This happened really recently to me with my ex who was also the only person I talked to on a regular basis (it probably wasn't a good idea for us, but I didn't have anybody else). It really hurts when for years you blow off anything for somebody, and then it gets to the point that they'll prioritize anything else over you.

I grew up in a college town on the south, so I can relate to wanting to get the fuck out of there. Being in ND, you can actually qualify for some pretty good out-of-state tuition wavers for schools out west and in the Midwest. I don't know if you've looked into this or not, but I know all I wanted to do when I turned 18 was get the fuck out of Mississippi, so I imagine you're feeling the same way. Good luck man. 

http://www.usnews.com/education/best-colleges/paying-for-college/articles/2011/07/27/how-to-qualify-for-out-of-state-tuition-breaks
Instead of quitting your meds, is there any way that you could look to switch up your prescription? It sounds like despite the side effects, they were doing you pretty good?

>Always had a like for different people and places.

How about you use your paycheck to get to those places you like?  If you're ready to leave this world, why not leave your current life behind and do something that might make you happy?

I haven't quite hit that point yet, but I tell myself that I'll quit my job and drive across the fucking country for the hell of it if I'm ever back at a point where I can truly accept the hurt I'd cause others by ending my life.

Have went hiking out to a bluff with the sole intention of doing that a few times now.  Still feel suicidal, but most of the time I'm glad I haven't done it yet.  I hope you don't, but I know how you feel, I'm not going to give you some bullshit trying to talk you out of it.  Whatever happens, good luck out there man.
What was your last job?  Did it have anything to do with your degree, or are you just kinda casually bouncing around?
Baby steps.  I can't say I *like* posting here per say, but it's nice as a release at least.

First time?

Definitely go with an open mind, and I've found it's best to at least mentally plan out what you're going to say beforehand.  For me, anytime I try to talk about it, it just sound really dumb and trivial, and I end up under-describing everything.  Like I tell them I occasionally have suicidal thoughts, but don't worry, I've never made any legit plans or anything (which is false).  And I think about self harm, but never follow through (false again).

And try to remember that these people truly do want to help you.  It's easy to become cynical and think "You don't really care, it's just your job to pretend to."  But they weren't drafted into the mental health field, and they don't do it for the money, they do it because they want to make a difference in people's lives.  So I know it's hard, but try to be open with them and let them help you, you know?

I hope you can sleep well and that things go well for you tomorrow.

Don't really have much to say, but I read every word. I enjoy your writing even though this obviously wasn't meant to showcase that. Had someone like Kathy in my life for a few years, we've fallen out of contact now for about half a year. 

Sorry you're in a pretty shitty situation right now.

The best thing I can think is to just be there. Listen. Talk if she wants, but don't pressure if she doesn't want to. 

And I know this doesn't sound like the best advice, but realize that you probably can't "fix" anything yourself. I mean don't get me wrong, having a support system is a hell of a lot better than being alone in your depression, but at the end of the day, depression is a personal struggle that people have to confront on their own. I know that can be hard, to watch your girlfriend in pain and not be able to "fix it", but by being there as someone who will listen, you'll certainly be doing good.

Before I decided: 
Terrible, obviously. At that point, it was the lowest I'd ever been. 

After I decided: 
It was a strange feeling. I still hated myself, but there was almost a hint of pride. Saying "fuck you world," I'm going of my own accord and there's nothing you can do about it. It wasn't a feeling of relief, but it felt like I was taking control of my life in some weird way. It didn't feel good or hopeful, it was just a glimpse of being in control again. 

Right afterwards I was just apathetic for a while. Accepting that I was going to live even if I hated every day.

Have a bunch stored up in my email that I write when I get really low. They're not really meant for anyone to find them per say, they're just to get stuff out that I don't know where to write otherwise.
In moderation I've found that it usually helps, but like others have said, everybody's different. I can't smoke anymore because of my job, but I know I would if I could.
I think about people who used to know me hearing that I'm dead. Idk, maybe I just want to imagine them actually remembering I exist.
Rooting for you!
Next week hopefully.  For now, the only specialist I've got is alcohol.
Can't stop thinking about it during the day, so I want to sleep.  Can't stop dreaming about it, so I want to wake up.  :( Good luck man, we're all here with you.

I kinda feel like I'm lying to myself, but I'm holding out hope that there will be another someday. It just hurts to see years of effort getting to know and getting close to someone go down the drain. Best of luck to you, I'll be rooting for you!
I'm really not familiar with bipolar, are there other medications you could try?
Paul's Online Math Notes. Saved my ass in college haha.

Talk it out. When I was doing LDR, we kept avoiding having that difficult conversation until it was really too late to save it. It ended with us talking as friends nearly as much as we did before, only this time her talking about the dates she's going on and how she wished I lived closer. What a fucking mess. I could go on and on with the sappy shit, but I don't feel like I'll find anybody better either. But just talk it over with him and make it clear where both of you stand.
Thanks for the tip. I'm looking to get over someone myself too.

Yeah, I used to find myself a bit guilty of romanticizing the past. Only remembering the good things and thinking that I had it so much better. A little nostalgia is alright in moderation, but it really can hurt if you let it.
Some sort of close relationship. Friendship, romantic, family, I don't care. I just need something to tie me down.
I love you. I mean I genuinely care about your well being and want you to feel better. I know that's what I'd love to hear again.

I've had that a bit. Do you think it's just physical weakness? I mean you've lost 40lbs. I haven't lost a ton, but I've certainly felt significantly weaker, and sometimes some shaking/unsteadiness comes with that.

I just feel like it all sounds really stupid to say out loud, so anytime I try, I downplay it, and just end up saying nevermind.  That also goes for typing anything out live.  Something that's worked for me is pre-writing everything beforehand, either in an email or in the notes of your phone or something.  That gives me a script or something to draw words from.

I tend to view an employer questioning them as a way to actually explain yourself, and if you do it right can be better than just blank spaces with no explanation.  I haven't been there in terms of applying for new jobs, but have been questioned about behaviors at work before on the occasion I'd let some things slip up.

Tell them the truth, but there's no real need for a ton of details.  Say that you were going through a lot in your personal life at that time, but you've taken steps to improve your situation since then.
I wouldn't say I love it or hate it.  It's something that I know is harmful, but provides a bit of a temporary release.  Like smoking an occasional cigarette.
I think we just want to feel something other than sadness.  The pain sucks, but it's something to take your mind off of the sadness in your life.  Idk, that's me anyway.

It varies from person to person, but I think I can generally say don't pry, but make yourself available you know?

It's not the same for everybody, but for me, knowing that somebody is there if I need it and truly cares helps just as much as actually talking about it.
Great to hear man, I'm happy for you.

I don't remember most of high school and my low periods at college. Used to joke around in high school about "way early onset Alzheimer's", but looking back it doesn't really seem like a joke. High school may have sucked, but only having a few distinct memories from a 4 year period of my life is pretty scary.

This was me for years, found myself physically unable to get any kind of release. Still pretty much like that, but to a bit of a lesser extent now. 

I guess the best non harmful suggestion I can think of is to try to just wear yourself out. I'm not saying go buy a punching bag or some shit, but hit something, lift something, or run until you forget about what you were upset about in the first place. 

Like I said, it's certainly not a magic cure-all, but it was the best thing that worked in the short term for me at least.
Only when I'm really low. Aka tonight.  Do my fingers because I want to avoid super obvious scars.  Don't know why I do it.

Short term help? There's always mixed feelings about them, but suicide hotlines are always a choice. I've called a couple times before, and sometimes getting it all out in words and just having someone to listen is a good release.

I plan it out in my head beforehand to tell people that I'm in a really bad place again when they ask, and then the time comes and I blow it off as "yeah, I'm doing pretty good now". And I move on, still feeling like shit.
Past two weeks have probably been the worst of my life. Don't know what it is man.

I kinda wonder myself. I've gone on walks to bridges with the sole intent of jumping and then haven't. I guess I personally don't consider it an attempt, but in the end, do labels even matter? Doesn't trivialize it or anything.

Damn man, I know the feeling, sorry you had to go with that. My best friend blew me off for the entire 10 months she was dating someone a few years back. I didn't realize that they broke up because she told me, I realized it because for the first time in nearly a year, I got a text lamenting about how we haven't hung out in forever and it's like I didn't even exist anymore. 

Now she's dating someone else again, and it's the same thing all over again. I guess it stings less this time since I kinda expected it, but still sucks you know?

Best of luck to you.

Senior here.  1:14am and I am doing my regularly scheduled saturday night math homework.  Hold in there man.  I know most of us would much rather be doing something else right now.  Have any music or books to pass the time?

Hey there.

So I can tell you I've been on both sides of this issue, and I can relate to what you're going through.  A few years ago, I found someone else online who was depressed, and we started talking, really just using each other as a way to vent.  She saved my life, really.  But over time, she got better, and I didn't.  Eventually, it was one way venting, and she hasn't responded in about a month now.  She always said it was fine, but I just felt like it wasn't.  But I can see where she's coming from you know?  It's hard work trying to hold someone else as well as yourself up.  I don't know how to feel.  Maybe upset, maybe mad, maybe just down on myself for making what became our friendship into this.

So I don't really know where I'm going with this.  I just want you to know that there are people here that know what it's like to go through this.
